title: Carpet Life by Household Size: Security Deposit Account Depreciation Table
content:
The carpet life used to depreciate a Security Deposit Account carpet replacement charge follows how many people lived in the home. The number of people is the count of approved occupants recorded on the Apartment Home Lease.

| Approved occupants on the lease | Carpet life |
|---|---|
| 4 or more | 48 months |
| exactly 3 | 54 months |
| fewer than 3 | the program's carpet useful life |

**Records read.** The approved occupants count on the Apartment Home Lease.

**Use.** The carpet life is the number of months of life that a carpet's remaining share is measured against. That share is the carpet life less the carpet's recorded age, never below 0, divided by the carpet life.

## Worked comparison (hypothetical carpet aged 24 months)

| Occupants | Carpet life | Remaining share |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 48 | 24 divided by 48, which is 0.5 |
| 4 | 48 | 0.5 |
| 3 | 54 | 30 divided by 54, which is 0.5555... |
| 2 | the program's carpet useful life | measured on that life |

**Boundary.** 3 occupants is the 54-month tier, and 4 occupants is the first count on the 48-month tier.
